content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Fall as Markets Await Data to Guide Fed
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields decline during early trade as market attention increasingly turns to the Federal Reserve's December meeting following a data hiatus during the government shutdown.  "Data releases starting this week should provide a clearer picture for one of the key risk over the coming weeks—the December Fed meeting," Jefferies' Mohit Kumar said in a note.  Jefferies is in the "bad news is good news camp" as any weakening in data would move the Fed closer to a December cut, the global economist said.

content.title: U.S. Treasuries Stabilize as Investors Stay Cautious Despite Government Reopening
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields stabilize in European mid-morning hours, having risen earlier on news that the U.S. government is set to reopen as caution creeps in.  "Markets remain cautious as attention shifts to the backlog of economic data soon to be released, which could paint a softer picture of the labor market and overall demand," says Exness' Eric Chia in a note.  The two-year Treasury yield rises 0.8 basis points to 3.573%; the 10-year Treasury yield is unchanged at 4.078%; and the 30-year yield stays steady at 4.662%, Tradeweb data show.

content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Decline on ADP's Weak Labor Market Signals
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields declined in early trade after payrolls firm ADP's estimate that the private sector was shedding 11,250 jobs a week in the four weeks through Oct. 25.  "With the U.S. federal government expected to reopen within days, delayed economic data will eventually be released and may give a clearer picture of the state of the U.S. economy ahead of the FOMC meeting in December," Danske Bank's Kristoffer Kjaer Lomholt said in a note.  Investors will watch out for Federal Reserve speakers as well as the Treasury's $42 billion auction of 10-year notes.

content.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Rise on Prospect of End to Government Shutdown
content.summary: U.S. Treasury yields were rising in Asian trade amid fresh optimism about seeing an end to the U.S. government shutdown soon. Late Sunday, the Senate cleared a key hurdle in its drive to end the record-long government shutdown, after Democrats provided enough votes to advance a measure aimed to end the impasse.
